# Model Architecture Modifications

Also called: NeRF Architecture Variants, Implicit Representation Modifications

## Overview
Model Architecture Modifications refer to structural changes applied to the standard Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) framework to address specific limitations such as geometric accuracy, rendering efficiency, dynamic scene handling, or input constraints. While the standard NeRF uses two Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to map 3D coordinates and viewing directions to volume density and color, this family encompasses methods that replace these MLPs with discrete structures (voxels, Gaussians), augment them with auxiliary heads (semantics, uncertainty), or condition them on external priors (vision transformers, physics simulations). These modifications enable capabilities ranging from real-time rendering and sparse-view synthesis to explicit surface reconstruction and dynamic scene modeling.

## Shared principles
The standard NeRF architecture [S6] serves as the baseline for most modifications. It consists of two Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs): a coarse network and a fine network. The coarse network takes positional encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$ and outputs a latent feature vector $\mathbf{h}$ and volume density $\sigma$. The fine network takes $\mathbf{h}$, positional encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$, and positional encoded view direction $\gamma(\mathbf{d})$ to output color $\mathbf{c}$ [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md].

$$
\gamma(\mathbf{x}, d_1, d_2) = [\mathbf{x}, \sin(2^{d_1}\pi\mathbf{x}), \cos(2^{d_1}\pi\mathbf{x}), \dots, \sin(2^{d_2-1}\pi\mathbf{x}), \cos(2^{d_2-1}\pi\mathbf{x})]
$$

Modifications generally fall into three categories [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md]:
1.  **Input Expansion:** Adding new conditioning vectors (e.g., appearance embeddings $\mathbf{z}_i$, fluid volume $v$, or previous stage RGB) to the input concatenation [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md].
2.  **Output Expansion:** Adding auxiliary heads to predict values other than $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{c}$, such as semantic labels $y_{aux}$, object codes $o$, or area encoding probabilities $p$. These are rendered using the same transmittance weights $T_i$ and opacity $\alpha_i$ as color:
    $$
    \hat{Y}(r) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i y_{aux}(x_i)
    $$
    [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md].
3.  **Representation Substitution:** Replacing the continuous MLP function with discrete structures (voxel grids, hash tables) or different implicit surfaces (SDFs) [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md].

## Subtopics

### [DoF-NeRF](9432-dof-nerf.md)
DoF-NeRF extends the standard NeRF to simulate depth-of-field effects by introducing learnable aperture ($K$) and focus distance ($F$) parameters per view, optimizing for all-in-focus 3D scenes from shallow DoF inputs. Choose this when input images have varying focus or when explicit lens simulation is required.

### [NeRF-VPT](11770-nerf-vpt.md)
NeRF-VPT uses a cascading view prompt tuning paradigm where RGB images from previous rendering stages serve as visual prompts for subsequent networks, progressively enhancing image quality without external networks. Choose this for iterative refinement in sparse-view settings.

### [Activation Feature Density Approximation](12492-activation-feature-density-approximation.md)
This method estimates volumetric density directly from intermediate activation features of the coarse MLP, replacing expensive fine network evaluations with lightweight statistical computations. Choose this to accelerate coarse-to-fine sampling without changing the underlying density formulation.

### [Signed Distance Function (SDF) Representations](12495-signed-distance-function-sdf-representations.md)
SDF representations replace the density field $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ with a continuous scalar field $s(\mathbf{x})$ representing distance to the nearest surface, enabling explicit surface extraction and sharper geometry. Choose this when geometric accuracy and surface normals are prioritized over soft volumetric boundaries.

### [Volume-Augmented NeRF](12973-volume-augmented-nerf.md)
Designed for dynamic fluid scenes, this variant binds an explicit fluid volume value $v_i$ to each sample point, allowing density and color to be learned based on differentiable fluid simulator outputs. Choose this for rendering dynamic fluids where standard static NeRF fails.

### [Neural-PIL Decomposition Architecture](12975-neural-pil-decomposition-architecture.md)
This architecture separates scene geometry, material properties (BRDF), and illumination into distinct networks, using a learned pre-integrated lighting network to render shaded colors. Choose this when input images have varying illumination and explicit reflectance decomposition is needed.

### [SAID-NeRF](13619-said-nerf.md)
SAID-NeRF exploits instance masks from Visual Foundation Models to enhance surface estimation of transparent objects by decomposing appearance into diffuse and specular components and enforcing semantic constraints. Choose this for transparent object reconstruction and robotic grasping applications.

### [MINE](13661-mine.md)
MINE models the source camera frustum using a continuous depth Multiplane Image (MPI) representation, conditioned on input images via a fully-convolutional decoder, allowing efficient rendering of multiple target views via homography warping. Choose this for efficient multi-view synthesis from a single source view.

### [Voxel and Sparse Grid Representations](13738-voxel-and-sparse-grid-representations.md)
These methods replace the continuous MLP with discrete spatial structures (dense voxels, sparse grids, hash tables) to store density and appearance features, enabling memory-efficient training and real-time rendering. Choose this for scalability to large scenes and real-time performance requirements.

### [Aleth-NeRF](13764-aleth-nerf.md)
Aleth-NeRF trains on under- and over-exposed images to render normal-light views by introducing 'Concealing Fields' that model light attenuation by air particles, operating on standard 8-bit LDR images. Choose this for low-light or high-dynamic-range scene synthesis without paired HDR data.

### [Transformer and Vision Model Integration](13911-transformer-and-vision-model-integration.md)
This family integrates Vision Transformers (ViT) and general Transformer architectures into NeRFs to leverage global semantic understanding and long-range dependencies, solving limitations of MLPs in single-image inputs or occlusions. Choose this for generalizable NeRFs or scenes requiring global context.

### [Human and Specific Subject Modeling](13997-human-and-specific-subject-modeling.md)
These methods adapt NeRF to model dynamic human subjects by integrating parametric human priors (e.g., SMPL) or structured latent codes anchored to deformable meshes, handling non-rigid deformation and occlusion. Choose this for novel view synthesis of humans or articulated subjects.

### [OPONeRF](14014-oponerf.md)
OPONeRF personalizes plenoptic mapping parameters for each sampled 3D point by dynamically conditioning network weights on the point's representation and scene features, handling test-time scene changes and perturbations. Choose this for robustness against motion, illumination changes, or contamination.

### [Mixer-NeRF](14073-mixer-nerf.md)
Mixer-NeRF addresses blurry details in standard NeRFs by introducing a hybrid spatial feature learning module (MLCA) and a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) network module to mix spatial and channel features before MLP inference. Choose this for high-frequency detail recovery.

### [Sparse View and Few-Shot Optimization](14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md)
This family addresses overfitting and geometry breakdown in sparse-view NeRFs through in-situ regularization, deformable sampling, or pseudo-observation densification, avoiding the need for large-scale pre-training. Choose this when input viewpoints are drastically reduced ($|S| < 20$).

### [Mixture-of-Experts and Modular Architectures](14429-mixture-of-experts-and-modular-architectures.md)
These architectures replace the single continuous function of NeRF with multiple specialized networks (experts) or parallel streams, partitioning the input domain to improve compression, speed, or capacity. Choose this for complex features or boundary discontinuity issues in grid-based INRs.

### [Uncertainty and Reliability](14487-uncertainty-and-reliability.md)
These methods extend NeRF to quantify prediction confidence by modeling the scene as a probabilistic entity, providing pixel-level reliability metrics for color and depth. Choose this for robust filtering and conformal prediction in sparse or unstructured data.

### [Object Decomposition and Composition](14518-object-decomposition-and-composition.md)
These methods explicitly separate a scene into distinct semantic or geometric object instances, enabling instance-level editing and amodal segmentation via auxiliary outputs like object codes. Choose this for structural decomposition and editing rather than just appearance labeling.

### [Lighting and Appearance Models](14522-lighting-and-appearance-models.md)
These models modify NeRF to explicitly represent illumination and material properties, separating albedo from illumination using global bases rather than implicit MLP learning. Choose this for relighting and handling varying lighting conditions.

### [Optimization and Training Procedures](14565-optimization-and-training-procedures.md)
This family covers algorithmic procedures for optimizing NeRFs, including structural modifications to the optimization scope such as skipping expensive fine-pass evaluations or restricting updates to specific layers. Choose this for efficient minimization of photometric loss under computational constraints.

### [Image Enhancement and Restoration Methods](14566-image-enhancement-and-restoration-methods.md)
These methods integrate restoration mechanisms (e.g., blur kernels, inpainting) into the NeRF loop to handle degraded inputs like blur, transient occlusions, or low resolution. Choose this when input imagery is not sharp or clean.

### [Modular, Hierarchical, and Latent Architectures](14567-modular-hierarchical-and-latent-architectures.md)
This family extends NeRF to handle non-rigid deformation with topological changes (e.g., HyperNeRF) or hierarchical scene structures (e.g., Strata-NeRF) using higher-dimensional spaces or discrete latent codes. Choose this for dynamic scenes with topology changes or stratified environments.

### [MuRF (Multi-Baseline Radiance Fields)](15007-murf-multi-baseline-radiance-fields.md)
MuRF is a feed-forward method for sparse view synthesis that constructs a target view frustum volume and uses a 3D context-aware convolutional decoder, effectively aggregating multi-view information even with small overlaps. Choose this for large baseline novel view synthesis.

### [Gaussian and Primitive-Based Representations](15011-gaussian-and-primitive-based-representations.md)
These methods replace the continuous MLP with discrete geometric primitives or explicit Gaussian distributions, improving rendering efficiency and geometric fidelity via alpha-blended primitives. Choose this for real-time rendering and explicit geometry.

### [Decentralized Federated NeRF](15032-decentralized-federated-nerf.md)
DecentNeRF learns global 3D scene representations from crowd-sourced images by distributing training to users and aggregating only global models, preventing personal data leakage. Choose this for privacy-preserving, large-scale scene reconstruction from distributed data.

### [Neural Proxy](15220-neural-proxy.md)
Neural Proxy represents photo-realistic targets as animatable proxies by injecting an animatable mesh proxy into the scene, combining neural volume rendering with neural texture. Choose this for synthesizing unseen animations without temporal learning.

### [ViSNeRF](15255-visnerf.md)
ViSNeRF efficiently synthesizes visualizations from dynamic volumetric scenes by combining explicit feature grids with implicit MLP decoders and generalized tensor factorization, reducing memory complexity. Choose this for high-dimensional $(3+K)$-D radiance fields.

### [EBAD-NeRF](15441-ebad-nerf.md)
EBAD-NeRF reconstructs sharp 3D radiance fields from motion-blurred images by jointly optimizing learnable camera poses and NeRF parameters using hybrid event-RGB data. Choose this for motion-blurred input recovery.

### [Point-NeRF Representation](15538-point-nerf-representation.md)
Point-NeRF replaces the continuous MLP with a discrete neural point cloud, avoiding ray sampling in empty space and leveraging classical point clouds for faster optimization. Choose this for efficient rendering with explicit geometric anchors.

### [NeurMiPs](15543-neurmips.md)
NeurMiPs represents a scene as a mixture of learnable rectangular planar surfaces, each acting as an independent expert, alleviating frontal-parallel limitations of traditional MPI. Choose this for high-efficiency rendering with superior extrapolation.

### [CodeNeRF](15544-codenerf.md)
CodeNeRF learns variation of object shapes and textures across a semantic category, enabling one-shot reconstruction of unseen objects from a single unposed input image by disentangling shape and texture embeddings. Choose this for few-shot or single-image novel view synthesis of object categories.

### [Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling](15546-dynamic-scene-and-temporal-modeling.md)
These methods extend static NeRF to reconstruct 4D space-time volumes, explicitly modeling temporal coordinates to handle non-rigid deformation and motion. Choose this for dynamic scenes changing over time.

### [NeRF-Casting](15547-nerf-casting.md)
NeRF-Casting integrates ray tracing into the NeRF pipeline to synthesize specular appearance and reflections by casting reflection rays into the NeRF geometry, avoiding the need for large MLPs to encode the environment. Choose this for photorealistic specular reflections.

### [RoseNeRF](15548-rosenerf.md)
RoseNeRF simplifies complex ray interactions inside transparent media to a single refraction event using a 4D light field representation and refraction network, avoiding IoR fields. Choose this for high-fidelity synthesis of real refractive objects.

### [NeRF-Det](15549-nerf-det.md)
NeRF-Det explicitly models scene geometry as an opacity field by jointly training a NeRF branch with a 3D detection pipeline, enabling end-to-end indoor 3D object detection. Choose this for joint reconstruction and detection tasks.

### [Semantic and Feature Field Extensions](15556-semantic-and-feature-field-extensions.md)
These extensions generalize NeRF by predicting arbitrary per-point feature signals (e.g., semantic labels, physical properties) in addition to color and density, lifting 2D supervision into 3D. Choose this for 3D-aware semantic understanding and zero-shot editing.

### [Neural Density-Distance Fields](15665-neural-density-distance-fields.md)
NeDDF reciprocally constrains distance and density fields, deriving density from depth values obtained via volume rendering, enabling boundaryless scenes and stable mesh extraction. Choose this for robust geometry and camera pose localization.

### [LAENeRF](15738-laenerf.md)
LAENeRF enables photorealistic and non-photorealistic local appearance editing of pre-trained NeRFs by learning a palette-based color decomposition within user-selected regions. Choose this for interactive local editing and stylization.

### [ExtremeNeRF](15739-extremenerf.md)
ExtremeNeRF achieves robust few-shot view synthesis under unconstrained, varying illumination by enforcing multi-view albedo consistency through a two-stage intrinsic decomposition pipeline. Choose this for sparse-view synthesis in challenging lighting.

### NeRF-VAE
**Definition:** A generative NeRF model that generalizes to out-of-distribution scenes and removes the need to train on each scene from scratch [S1].
**Steps:** The NeRF renderer is conditioned on a latent code trained using Iterative Amortized Inference and a ResNet encoder. An attention-based scene function is introduced instead of the typical MLP [S1].
**Comparison:** Outperforms baseline NeRF with a low number of scene views (5-20), but is outperformed by baseline NeRF when a large number of views are available (100+) due to lower scene expressivity [S1].

### PIE-NeRF
**Definition:** A pipeline integrating physics-based elastodynamic simulation with a neural radiance field representation, using a meshless discretisation based on quadratic generalized moving least squares on top of the density field of a NeRF [S1].
**Steps:** Enables large deformations and nonlinear hyperelastic material simulation directly on the implicit representation and supports interactive manipulation of real-world captured scenes with complex geometries [S1].

### DäRF Implementation Details
**Parameters:** NeRF Backbone: K-planes [36]. MDE Model: DPT-hybrid [38]. Optimizer: Adam [21]. NeRF Learning Rate: 1e-2. MDE Learning Rate: 1e-5. LR Schedule: Cosine warmup [S2, unofficial].

### NeRF Model Architecture
**Definition:** The neural network architecture for NeRF, consisting of dense layers with ReLU activations, potentially using view directions as input [S3, unofficial].
**Parameters:** `D`: The depth of the network (number of hidden layers). Default is 8. `input_ch_views`: The number of input channels for view directions. Default is 3. `output_ch`: The number of output channels. Default is 4 (RGB + density). `use_viewdirs`: Boolean flag to determine if view directions are used as input to the network [S3, unofficial].

### S3-NeRF
**Definition:** A method using shadow and shading cues to infer scene geometry and enable single-image NeRF training [S1].
**Steps:** Employ a UNISURF-based occupancy field 3D representation instead of density. Use a modified physics-based rendering equation. Use occupancy-based shadow calculation [S1].

### NeuralEditor
**Definition:** A method employing a point cloud-guided NeRF model for shape manipulation, leveraging K-D trees and deterministic integration strategy for accurate point cloud-based rendering, with Phong reflection modeling to enhance color fidelity and geometric detail [S4].
**Steps:** 1. Employ point cloud-guided NeRF model. 2. Leverage K-D trees. 3. Use deterministic integration strategy. 4. Achieve accurate point cloud-based rendering. 5. Apply Phong reflection modeling [S4].

### Network Architectures
**Parameters:** MLPs A and F use the MLP designed in NeRF, with hidden layer sizes increased from 256 to 384. MLPs A and F are not used during inference, allowing more time on training. Small MLP H is the same as the small MLP used in SNeRG, with two hidden layers, each consisting 16 neurons [S5].

### NeRF-Swin
**Definition:** A baseline method that performs super-resolution on an LR NeRF using released SwinIR models under the 'Real-World Image Super-Resolution' setting, trained on more than 10k LR-HR pairs [S6].
**Parameters:** Training set size: More than 10k LR-HR pairs [S6].
**Pitfalls:** On synthetic Blender dataset, SwinIR may produce false predictions due to domain mismatch. On real-world LLFF dataset, SwinIR tends to be oversmooth and may predict false color or geometry [S6].
**Metrics:** Blender ×2 (100x100): PSNR 26.34, SSIM 0.913, LPIPS 0.075. Blender ×4 (100x100): PSNR 24.85, SSIM 0.881, LPIPS 0.108. Blender ×2 (200x200): PSNR 28.03, SSIM 0.926, LPIPS 0.058. Blender ×4 (200x200): PSNR 26.78, SSIM 0.906, LPIPS 0.086. LLFF ×2: PSNR 25.18, SSIM 0.793, LPIPS 0.147. LLFF ×4: PSNR 23.26, SSIM 0.685, LPIPS 0.247 [S6].

## Background
The standard NeRF architecture, introduced by Mildenhall et al. [1], established the paradigm of representing 3D scenes as continuous volumetric functions using MLPs. Subsequent research has rapidly diversified the architecture to address specific challenges such as training speed, geometric fidelity, dynamic scenes, and sparse inputs. The field has evolved from simple MLP modifications to complex hybrid systems involving transformers, discrete grids, and physics-based simulations.
